stem: Which range of products and services is covered under the European Accessibility Act (Directive 2019/882)?

options.text: Prescription medical devices, hospital patient monitors, and specialized clinical diagnostic health equipment.
options.rationale: Medical devices, clinical monitors, and specialized diagnostic healthcare equipment are regulated separately under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR), not the European Accessibility Act.

options.text: Residential housing architecture, municipal pedestrian walkways, and physical brick-and-mortar commercial buildings.
options.rationale: The EAA does not establish mandatory EU-wide harmonized standards for physical architecture or the built environment; regulating physical buildings was left to the discretion of individual member states.

options.text: Traditional domestic household appliances, including analog kitchen cooking stoves, refrigerators, and washing machines.
options.rationale: The EAA specifically targets digital computing hardware, telecommunications, self-service terminals, and electronic services; traditional domestic white goods are excluded from its scope.

options.text: Key consumer digital products and services, including ATMs, smartphones, e-books, e-commerce, and online banking.
options.rationale: Under Article 2 of Directive 2019/882, the EAA specifically targets key private-sector consumer hardware (smartphones, computers, ATMs, ticketing machines, e-readers) and digital services (e-commerce, banking, passenger transport interfaces, and e-books).

explanation: The European Accessibility Act (Directive 2019/882) harmonizes accessibility requirements across the EU internal market for a targeted list of private-sector consumer products and services. Its scope covers consumer hardware (computers, operating systems, smartphones, ATMs, ticketing and check-in kiosks, e-readers) and consumer services (e-commerce, consumer banking, e-books, and digital passenger transport interfaces). It does not mandate harmonized rules for the physical built environment, nor does it cover medical devices or domestic household appliances.
